items.title: Ivanti patches two more Connect Secure zero-days chained in attacks
items.snippet: Ivanti released security updates to patch two more Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway flaws that have been chained in zero-day attacks since at least October 1. [...]
items.summary: Ivanti released updates for two Connect Secure remote-access gateway flaws that it says have been chained in zero-day attacks since at least October 1.
items.why: Apply the updates and check Connect Secure systems for signs of exploitation.

items.title: FBI links $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist to North Korean hackers
items.snippet: The FBI has confirmed that North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor were behind the $6.3 billion crypto-theft attack on Binance, making it the largest cryptocurrency heist on record. [...]
items.summary: The FBI says North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor carried out the $6.3 billion Binance crypto theft.
items.why: Review cryptocurrency custody and transaction controls; the snippet does not identify the attack method.

items.title: Polymarket Returns $3.9 Million to Traders as DebugBear Cites DNS Hijack
items.snippet: DebugBear says its DNS records were compromised via its domain registrar, and early findings show a single customer was targeted. The post Polymarket Returns $3.9 Million to Traders as DebugBear Cites DNS Hijack appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.summary: DebugBear says attackers compromised its DNS records through its domain registrar; early findings indicate one customer was targeted.
items.why: Review registrar access and DNS changes, and investigate whether users were redirected.

items.title: FBI Flags Over 600 Addresses Tied to North Korea’s Binance Heist
items.snippet: The FBI has officially pinned the $6 billion Binance hack on North Korea’s TraderTraitor as the attackers launder the stolen crypto. The post FBI Flags Over 600 Addresses Tied to North Korea’s Binance Heist appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.summary: The FBI says more than 600 addresses are tied to North Korea’s Binance heist as attackers launder stolen cryptocurrency.
items.why: Check whether relevant addresses appear in transaction monitoring and apply current screening controls.

items.title: New VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi AI to Rank Victims by Financial Value
items.snippet: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER (aka VOLTA) that makes use of a large language model (LLM) to rank a victim's stolen data by their monetization value. Like other typical stealer families, VOLTA is equipped to harvest passwords and cookies from Chromium-
items.summary: Researchers say VOLTA infostealer uses a large language model to rank stolen victim data by potential monetization value.
items.why: Review endpoint alerts for infostealer activity and investigate suspected credential or data theft.

items.title: FBI blames N. Korea’s TraderTraitor for Binance theft, urges crypto industry to block transactions
items.snippet: The FBI and U.S. Secret Service alleged this weekend that North Korean hackers were responsible for stealing more than $6.3 billion from cryptocurrency platform Binance last week.
items.summary: The FBI and U.S. Secret Service allege North Korean hackers were responsible for stealing more than $6.3 billion from Binance.
items.why: Crypto organizations should review transaction monitoring and consider the FBI’s call to block transactions.

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources Super-Agent, a coding agent that watches team chats for work
items.snippet: Deepseek released a research prototype of dsh-superagent, a coding agent that does work on a GitHub repository for you. Who can ask for work The agent gets to work in two situations: an allowed user asks for something, or a rule your team wrote covers it. You can also open up a chat or GitHub scope, and then anyone in
items.summary: DeepSeek released a research prototype of a coding agent that can work on a GitHub repository when an allowed user or team rule requests it.
items.why: Review who can authorize agent work and what repository permissions it receives.

items.title: The first ten lines of a command policy for AI coding agents
items.snippet: In this Help Net Security interview, Vinay Thakker, CTO of KloudStax, explains how to set identity, credentials, and network limits for AI agents. He argues that agents should run under their own identity, with the person’s identity attached when acting on someone’s behalf. He covers where credential proxies go wrong,
items.summary: A KloudStax executive explains how to set identity, credentials, and network limits for AI agents, arguing they should have their own identity.
items.why: Give agents distinct identities and restrict their credentials and network access.

items.title: Byoky: Open-source wallet for AI API keys
items.snippet: Byoky is an open-source wallet for AI API keys, available as a Chrome and Firefox extension and as iOS and Android apps. Users store their keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini and other providers in it, encrypted on their own device. Apps that want those keys ask the wallet for access, and the wallet sends each re
items.summary: Byoky is an open-source app for storing AI API keys encrypted on a device, available as browser extensions and mobile apps.
items.why: Assess how keys are stored and which apps can access them before adopting a key wallet.

items.title: Product showcase: Trust Onion uses rotating codewords to verify callers
items.snippet: Trust Onion is a free app that gives trusted groups three rotating codewords to check who they are communicating with. It also includes signed selfies, message checks, and callback requests. It is available for macOS, iOS, and Android. I tested the iPhone app with an older person, exploring setup and the tools availabl
items.summary: Trust Onion is an app that uses rotating codewords to help groups verify callers; it also offers signed selfies, message checks, and callback requests.
items.why: Consider independent caller verification for trusted groups communicating through potentially uncertain channels.

She delves into the Pentagon’s disputes with SpaceX and Anthrop
items.summary: A War on the Rocks discussion asks what happens when the military depends on technologies it does not own, drawing on a book about Big Tech and war.
items.why: The discussion raises how reliance on privately owned technology may shape military capabilities.

Sirehna, a subsidiary of Naval Group, offered a rare opportunity to the 25 journalists representing 16 nationalities who attended the tour: a live
items.summary: Naval Group’s Sirehna demonstrated the SEAQUEST-S, a multi-role combat uncrewed surface vessel designed for deployment from warships.
items.why: The demonstration highlights a surface vessel designed to operate from warships.

items.title: Australia unveils secretive Ghost Shark underwater drone payloads
items.snippet: The Australian Navy recently lifted the veil on some payloads the service is fielding on its Ghost Shark extra-large autonomous underwater vehicles.
items.summary: The Australian Navy disclosed some payloads it is fielding on its Ghost Shark extra-large autonomous underwater vehicles.
items.why: The disclosed payloads offer a glimpse of equipment used on autonomous underwater vehicles.

items.title: Rafale M Conducts Maiden Trials onboard Indian Aircraft Carrier INS Vikrant
items.snippet: The maiden landing of the French Rafale M fighter on INS Vikrant occurred on October 29, 2026. The landing was successful in the maiden attempt... The post Rafale M Conducts Maiden Trials onboard Indian Aircraft Carrier INS Vikrant appeared first on Naval News .
items.summary: A French Rafale M made its maiden landing on India’s INS Vikrant, succeeding on its first attempt, Naval News reports.
items.why: The trial demonstrates carrier operations involving a French fighter and an Indian aircraft carrier.

items.title: Russian Navy Cancels Modernization of Kirov-Class Battlecruiser Pyotr Velikiy
items.snippet: The Russian Navy has canceled modernization plans for the Kirov-class battlecruiser Pyotr Velikiy. Read how budget constraints are reshaping Russia's surface fleet. The post Russian Navy Cancels Modernization of Kirov-Class Battlecruiser Pyotr Velikiy appeared first on Naval News .
items.summary: Naval News reports that the Russian Navy canceled modernization plans for the Kirov-class battlecruiser Pyotr Velikiy.
items.why: The cancellation is relevant to assessments of plans for Russia’s surface fleet.

items.title: Ryanair may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
items.snippet: The airline says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless there is an end to the US-Israel war with Iran.
items.summary: Ryanair says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless the US-Israel war with Iran ends; the airline may freeze workers’ pay and raise fares.
items.why: The airline’s statement links fuel costs to the war, with potential implications for fares and pay.

items.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack
items.snippet: The exchange froze transactions following the incident which has been linked to a North Korean group.
items.summary: Binance froze transactions after the largest-ever crypto hack, which has been linked to a North Korean group; users withdrew $3.6bn.
items.why: The withdrawals and transaction freeze show how a crypto incident can affect exchange activity.

items.title: Don’t Read Too Much Into These Midterms
items.snippet: Voters are angry about the Iran war, but that doesn’t mean they want to go back to the pre-Trump status quo.
items.summary: Foreign Policy argues that anger about the Iran war among voters does not necessarily mean they want a return to the pre-Trump status quo.
items.why: The article cautions against treating opposition to a war as evidence of broader political preference.

items.title: The Biggest October Surprise of All
items.snippet: A crisis that brought the U.S. and the Soviets to the brink of nuclear war in 1962 reshaped U.S. politics.
items.summary: Foreign Policy says a crisis that brought the U.S. and the Soviets close to nuclear war in 1962 reshaped U.S. politics.
items.why: The story links a nuclear crisis to subsequent political change in the United States.

items.title: Germany news: Berlin hosts digital summit with AI focus
items.snippet: A government-run conference is to look at the uses and dangers of artificial intelligence. This comes as the German and UK defense ministers will discuss expanding AI's role in military cooperation. DW has more.

learn.explainer: DNS records connect a domain name with information used to direct internet traffic. If records are changed without authorization, users may be sent somewhere other than the intended destination.
A USV is an uncrewed surface vessel: a vessel that operates on the water without a crew aboard. The SEAQUEST-S is described as a multi-role combat USV designed for deployment from warships.
The Strait of Hormuz is a shipping passage discussed here as dangerous and costly, despite U.S. claims that it is open. Assessments of its status can matter to shipping decisions.

analysis.headline: Dependencies and disruptions across digital and physical systems
paragraphs: Several stories center on dependencies that can become points of exposure. Ivanti’s gateway flaws were chained in attacks, while DebugBear says its DNS records were compromised through its registrar. The Binance stories describe theft, transaction controls and withdrawals, with authorities attributing the incident to North Korean hackers.

The military technology discussion raises a related question: what happens when armed forces depend on technology they do not own? The SEAQUEST-S demonstration and Ghost Shark payloads offer examples of systems and equipment entering military use, while the AI summit brings civilian and defense applications into view.

For defenders, the cyber reports suggest checking patch status, registrar controls and transaction monitoring rather than assuming one safeguard is enough. For analysts, the stories point to the value of tracing dependencies and separating confirmed details from claims. The Hormuz report also underscores that assessments of access and risk can differ.
takeaways: Prioritize gateway updates and review DNS control paths.
Treat crypto incident response as both a security and operational concern.
Track how reliance on external technology shapes military systems.
